Derek Neldner

CEO and Group Head, RBC Capital Markets & Co-Head, Global Transaction Banking

Back to Leadership

Derek Neldner is CEO and Group Head, RBC Capital Markets & Co-Head, Global Transaction Banking is a member of RBC’s Group Executive. Derek has global oversight of the firm and, along with the Capital Markets Operating Committee, sets the growth strategy for RBC’s Corporate & Investment Banking and Global Markets business activities worldwide. Together with other members of Group Executive, Derek is also responsible for setting the overall strategic direction of RBC.

In addition to his leadership role with RBC Capital Markets, Derek is also a board member for RBC US Group Holdings LLC, RBC Dominion Securities Inc. and the RBC Foundation.

Derek joined RBC in 1995 and has held a broad array of responsibilities across the firm and served as Global Head of Investment Banking prior to his current role. He has significant experience across all aspects of investment banking including mergers and acquisitions, debt and equity financing, and he continues to provide senior coverage and advice to a number of the firm’s most significant clients.

Derek has a longstanding commitment to philanthropy and giving back to the community. In addition to his role on the Business Advisory Counsel for the University of Alberta, School of Business, he also currently volunteers with a variety of charitable organizations including serving as a member of the 2023 United Way Campaign Cabinet as Finance Sector Chair and Board Member of The Hospital for Sick Children (SickKids) foundation.

Derek holds a Bachelor of Commerce degree in Finance from the University of Alberta and is a Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA), as designated by the CFA Institute. Derek is married with four children and lives in Toronto, Canada.

Manish Bhandari

Senior Vice President & Chief Financial Officer

Back to Leadership

Manish Bhandari is Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer of RBC Capital Markets. In his role, Manish leads the Finance teams for Capital Markets globally and has responsibility for providing strategic counsel to the business and its senior executive team, promoting a robust financial controls and management culture, and enabling long-term value creation. He also has oversight for financial and performance management frameworks and policies for Capital Markets. Manish is a member of both the Capital Markets and CFO Group Operating Committees.

Manish has more than 20 years of deep institutional and consumer banking experience with cross-functional leadership across lines of business, risk and finance. Prior to joining RBC, he was Chief Financial Officer of MUFG Americas with responsibility for finance and strategy for the Americas Wholesale Business across Banking, Markets and Transactional Banking, overseeing multiple legal entities, regulatory jurisdictions as well as operational process improvements. Prior to this, Manish held progressively senior roles with Citigroup, including as Chief Financial Officer of its Global Corporate and Investment Bank, where he applied a client centric mindset across financial controls, strategy, innovation and regulatory policies.

Manish earned his Bachelor of Science in Petrochemical Engineering from the University of Pune in India, and his MBA from Thunderbird, the American Graduate School of International Management.

Celine Boffo

Senior Vice President, Human Resources

Back to Leadership

Celine Boffo is SVP, HR for RBC Capital Markets where she leads the design and execution of an integrated talent strategy for the business globally. She sits on the Operating Committee (OC) for Capital Markets and the Human Resources OC.

Celine has built her career on a foundation of business transformation, people strategies and organizational effectiveness. Her passion for developing and executing impactful people, talent and culture strategies brought her to RBC HR in 2013 and she has since held a number of senior positions including Head of HR for the 25,000 advisors and leaders serving clients across RBC’s Canadian Personal and Commercial Banking distribution network and VP, Talent Management where she was globally responsible for executive and high potential employee development as well as diversity and inclusion in leadership. In her previous role, she led the global HR team supporting RBC’s Wealth Management and Insurance businesses across 3 continents.

Before starting her corporate career with CGI, a Canadian IT services firm with global operations, she earned her Ph.D. in Management from HEC Montreal. At CGI, Celine headed up the organizational change management center of expertise and consulted on organizational design, development and change across industries. She then led enterprise-wide change management and governance programs at Rogers Communications before returning to consulting.

Celine is a Board member of Easter Seals Canada, a charitable organization that provides services and support to promote access, inclusion and opportunities to Canadians living with disabilities.

Trevor Gardner

Head, Global Investment Banking Coverage

Back to Leadership

Trevor Gardner is Head of Global Investment Banking Coverage and a member of the Capital Markets Operating Committee at RBC Capital Markets. With more than 25 years of capital markets experience at RBC, Trevor has held roles across Investment Banking and Equity Capital Markets in Toronto and Calgary. He was previously Head of Canadian Investment Banking and Co-Head of Canadian Energy Investment Banking.

Trevor brings extensive experience advising clients on a broad range of transactions, including mergers and acquisitions as well as debt and equity financing. He is actively engaged in senior client coverage and provides advice to clients across industries.

Trevor is an executive member of RBC Capital Markets' Canadian Diversity Leadership Council. Beyond his professional responsibilities, Trevor is deeply involved in community initiatives, serving as Chair of Right To Play's Canadian Advisory Board and Chair of the Board of Directors for YMCA Calgary. He is also a member of the Dean's Advisory Council for the Lazaridis School of Business and Economics at Wilfrid Laurier University.

Originally from Saskatchewan, Trevor holds a Bachelor of Business Administration (Honours) from Wilfrid Laurier University and is a Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA).

Bobby Grubert

Head, AI and Digital Innovation

Back to Leadership

Bobby Grubert is the Head of AI and Digital Innovation for RBC Capital Markets. In this role, Bobby leads the firm’s end-to-end AI and digital innovation strategy to deliver transformative client solutions, drive scale and accelerate adoption across the firm to enable the Capital Markets business to compete in a digital world. He is responsible for embedding AI-driven technologies and capabilities as core drivers of client value and revenue growth with tangible commercial and measurable outcomes.

Prior to this position, Bobby was instrumental in driving the electronification of RBC’s Global Markets franchise, fostering innovation and prioritizing AI for commercial growth. He also played a key role in implementing Aiden, an award-winning algorithmic trading platform, in partnership with RBC Borealis. Bobby began his career at RBC as an energy trader in 1996 and has since held multiple senior roles across the organization.

Bobby is a member of the RBC Capital Markets Operating Committee and founding member of the RBC U.S. Capital Markets Diversity Leadership Council. He lectures MBAs and Executives at MIT Sloan and serves as an Executive Board Member and Chairman Emeritus, Ronald McDonald House NY.

Andrew Hammond

Executive Vice President, Commercial & Wholesale Credit Risk

Back to Leadership

As EVP Commercial & Wholesale Credit Risk within Group Risk Management, Andrew leads the team responsible for the global oversight of wholesale credit risk originated by RBC Capital Markets, Commercial Banking and City National Bank.  As the Chief Risk Officer for RBC Capital Markets, Andrew and his team are responsible for driving strong risk governance practices aligned with enterprise standards, promoting a strong risk culture and providing risk insights and understanding to the business. Andrew is a member of the Group Risk Management and RBC Capital Markets Operating Committees.

Andrew has held progressively senior roles across GRM and RBC over his 20 years with the bank. In his previous role as SVP, Global Head of Market & Counterparty Credit Risk, he was responsible for the enterprise-wide oversight and governance of market, counterparty credit, liquidity risk and interest rate risk, as well as global model risk management and validation. Prior to that, Andrew led Enterprise Risk and acted as COO for the GRM function, and before that led the Global Credit and Cash Management Group in RBC Wealth Management. 

Andrew’s earlier roles in GRM included the oversight of all risks arising for Wealth Management businesses in the Americas. Additionally, Andrew has provided risk support to Capital Markets’ Corporate Banking and Global Markets platforms in Toronto and London.

Andrew joined RBC in 2005 after completing his MBA at the Schulich School of Business at York University with a specialization in Finance. He also holds a Bachelor of Fine Arts from Toronto Metropolitan University.

Dominic Hudson

Head, Investment Banking, Europe and APAC

Back to Leadership

Dominic Hudson leads our investment banking sector, product and country teams across Europe and APAC, and is a member of the RBC Capital Markets Operating Committee.

Dominic is responsible for executing the regional growth strategy for our investment banking franchises in Europe and APAC, focused on achieving our client, revenue and market share goals, building upon our existing robust client franchise and deepening our incredibly strong bench of talent.

Dominic began his career as a chartered accountant at Ernst & Young. Head, Global Markets

Back to Leadership

Jonathan Hunter is Head of Global Markets for RBC Capital Markets, and has been a member of the RBC Capital Markets Operating Committee since 2008. He is also on the board of RBC’s U.S. Intermediate Holding Company (IHC).

Jonathan has been with RBC for more than 30 years, joining its Dealer Trainee Program in 1991. Jonathan recently completed an eight-year term as a member of the Board of the International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA).

Jonathan is also actively involved in RBC’s diversity, mentorship and recruitment initiatives, and is a member of RBC Capital Markets’ Canadian Diversity Leadership Council. In 2018, he was formally recognized by the Women in Capital Markets organization as a Champion of Change in acknowledgement for his ongoing efforts to advance women in the workplace.

In addition, Jonathan is a key participant and contributor in RBC’s many community and charitable initiatives, including the RBC Race for the Kids, RBC Trade for the Kids, and he serves as a member of the United Way’s Major Individual Givers cabinet as part of RBC’s annual Employee Giving Campaign.

With Jonathan’s focus on digital transformation, he was recently named to the Advisory Board of the newly designed Smith’s Master of Financial Innovation & Technology (MFIT) program at Queen’s University. He also served as Chair of the Board of Trustees, and sat on the Board of Governors, for The Bishop Strachan School in Toronto from 2015 to 2021.

Jonathan earned his Honours Bachelor of Commerce Degree (Finance) from Queen’s University in 1991, and is a Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA).

Sian Hurrell is Co-CEO of RBC Europe Limited, Head of Capital Markets Europe and Global Head of Sales, Relationship Management & Structuring.

As Co-CEO, Sian drives the strategic direction and oversight of the bank's European Capital Markets and Wealth Management businesses, spanning multiple jurisdictions and bringing together RBC's global capabilities to deliver integrated solutions for clients. As Head of Capital Markets Europe, Sian oversees a platform that combines deep regional expertise in Investment Banking, Corporate Banking and Global Markets, with the scale of a top 10 global investment bank. Capital Markets Europe serves major corporates, financial sponsors, Sovereigns, Supranationals and Agencies (SSAs), insurance companies, banks, asset managers and hedge funds, bringing together advice, capital, liquidity provision and market access to help clients achieve their objectives.

Patti Perras Shugart is Head of Global Corporate Banking and a member of the Operating Committee at RBC Capital Markets. In her role, Patti oversees a team of approximately 600 professionals globally who specialize in lending, trading credit, loan portfolio management and transaction banking for our corporate and institutional clients. She also chairs the Loan Portfolio Review Committee and the Commitments Committee which determine the firm’s global lending decisions.

Patti is a strong advocate for diversity and inclusion. She sits on the firm’s Capital Markets Global Diversity Leadership Council, is a co-founder of RWomen, a global internal forum dedicated to fostering and developing female talent, and she chairs VersaFi’s Advisory Council. She is RBC’s Executive Sponsor for the United Way’s Women United group, is a past United Way Cabinet Member, and a past Executive Champion for the Toronto RBC Race for the Kids. Patti has been recognized for her outstanding contributions to the industry through the VersaFi Visionary Award in 2025, the Champion of Change Award in 2016, and the Award for Leadership in 2010. She was also named one of Canada's Top 100 Most Powerful Women by Women's Executive Network in both 2015 and 2017.

Patti has an MBA from the University of Toronto (Rotman) and a Bachelor of Commerce (Honours) from Queen’s University.

Back to Leadership
Vito Sperduto

U.S. Head, RBC Capital Markets U.S.

Back to Leadership

Vito Sperduto is the Head of RBC Capital Markets U.S. and a member of the Global Capital Markets Operating Committee. He collaborates closely with RBCCM’s global business heads to develop, align, and execute business strategies for sustained growth across all of RBCCM’s businesses. Acting as a strategic and trusted advisor to his clients, Vito leverages his considerable relationships and experience to help them achieve their business goals. He promotes cross-business coordination and collaboration in support of RBCCM’s overall strategy and works diligently to advance RBC’s pan-U.S. initiatives. Vito also focuses on RBCCM’s brand building, talent development, and mentoring initiatives. He is especially passionate about helping local communities prosper through his extensive charitable endeavors.

Vito has over 30 years of investment banking experience and has advised on over 200 transactions valued at over $250 billion. Prior to his current role, he was the Global Head of Mergers and Acquisitions, responsible for the firm’s overall M&A efforts across all sectors. Vito has extensive experience in originating and executing transactions in general industrials and diversified services (with a focus on aerospace, defense, and government services), communications, media and entertainment, technology, business services, and consumer and retail sectors.

Before joining RBCCM, Vito was a Managing Director and Head of Software M&A coverage for CIBC World Markets in New York, where he worked across the defense, consumer, business services, and technology sectors. He previously worked for SoundView Technology Group, Smith Barney, and Kidder, Peabody.

Vito is a member of RBC’s Global Capital Markets Operating Committee, U.S. Executive Committee, U.S. Regional Operating Committee and the board of RBC Capital Markets, LLC. He is an active leader of RBC’s community service programs, including serving as captain of RBC's New York Race for the Kids and co-executive sponsor of RBC PRIDE USA. Vito is the Chairman of the Board of Play Rugby USA, an organization that uses rugby as a tool to mentor over 5,500 NYC children ages 8 to 18. He earned his A.B. from Harvard University in Computer Science/Engineering Sciences.

Matthew R. Stopnik

Global Head, Investment Banking

Back to Leadership

Matthew Stopnik is Head of Global Investment Banking. He joined RBC Capital Markets in January 2015 as the Co-Head of Financial Sponsors and was appointed Co-Head of U.S. Investment Banking in 2018. Since then, Matthew and Jim Wolfe have successfully progressed the U.S. Investment Banking strategy by recruiting and developing talent, growing our advisory franchise, further balancing our GIB product mix, and expanding market share.

In addition to establishing and driving the strategy for our Global Investment Banking business, Matthew also manages RBC’s relationships with some of the largest and most active private equity firms in the world. Matthew serves on the firm’s Capital Markets and U.S. Regional Operating Committees and is a member of the firm’s Commitments Committee.

Prior to joining RBC, Matthew spent 20 years at UBS Investment Bank where his most recent role was serving as its U.S. Head of Financial Sponsors. Matthew is Vice Chair and a member of the Board of Trustees of the TEAK Fellowship, and a David Rockefeller Fellow of the Partnership for New York City. He received a B.A from the University of Michigan. Matthew and his wife live in New York City with their two children.

Allison Szmulewicz

Chief Operating Officer

Back to Leadership

Allison Szmulewicz is Chief Operating Officer of RBC Capital Markets with global responsibility for operations, transformation, as well as risk and control. In her role, she oversees the Capital Markets platform, ensuring  the delivery of a best-in-class experience for clients, while evolving constantly to meet business priorities and regulatory requirements in a dynamic and ever-changing environment.

Allison brings over 20 years of experience from Citi, where she held various senior leadership roles spanning technology, operations and transformation. As Head of Banking & International & Client Technology, she led the delivery of client-facing digital interactions, streamlined banking processes through the use of customer relationship management (CRM) and know-your-customer (KYC) systems, and oversaw technology deployments across over 90 countries. Prior to that role, Allison was Head of Operations and Technology for Latin America, driving key transformation programs on automation / manual process reduction. She had also held global leadership positions including Global Head of Transformation as well as Interim Head of Global Operations. Before Citi, Allison managed the client marketing team at Lazard Frères Asset Management, where she created high volume client materials and played a key role in launching the firm’s first online client offering.

Allison holds a Bachelor of Science in Business Administration (BSBA) degree in International Business from American University, in Washington, D.C., with a concentration in Marketing and a Minor in French. She currently resides in New Jersey with her family.

Back to Leadership
Jim Wolfe

Head, Global Investment Banking Capital Markets

Back to Leadership

Jim Wolfe is Head of Global Investment Banking Capital Markets, overseeing the firm’s financing products across debt and equity in both the public and private markets.

Prior to assuming his current role in May 2024, Jim served as Co-Head of U.S. Investment Banking from 2018-2024, where he shared responsibility for the coverage of banking clients and prospects, as well as oversight of the industry sector coverage groups, mergers and acquisitions, equity capital markets, leveraged finance and loan and high-yield capital markets teams.

From 2008 to 2018, Jim was responsible for the firm’s leveraged finance business in the U.S and Europe, leading an experienced team of specialized professionals in raising capital for corporate acquisitions, leveraged buyouts, recapitalizations and refinancings. Jim also serves on the Global Capital Markets Operating Committee and is a member of the firm’s Commitments and Underwriting Distribution Committees. He joined RBC in June 2008 after a 15-year tenure at Bear Stearns where he served as a Senior Managing Director in the Leveraged Finance Group.

With over 32 years of experience, Jim has successfully executed transactions of all sizes across a broad range of industry sectors.

Jim holds a B.S. in Accounting from the University of Southern California and an MBA from The Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania. He served on the Board of Trustees at Greens Farms Academy in Westport, CT, from 2012 to 2018, and alongside his wife, chaired the Parents Executive Committee of Bowdoin College from 2014 to 2019.

Michael Cook

Vice Chair

Back to Leadership

Michael Cook is Vice Chairman of Global Investment Banking, RBC Capital Markets Australia. Michael serves as a senior ambassador of RBC Capital Markets, working closely with the investment banking team to build relationships with clients in Australia.

Michael brings considerable experience and an extensive network to RBC. He spent 19 years with Macquarie in a number of senior roles and 15 years with Bankers Trust, which Macquarie acquired in 1999.

During his time at Macquarie, Michael was appointed Head of Corporate Advisory and Co-Head of Corporate Finance, which ultimately became Macquarie Capital. He also spent seven years with Macquarie in New York with a focus on building the firm's private equity buy-side and infrastructure businesses. On his return to Australia in 2014, Michael chaired Macquarie’s Client Coverage Group with a broad sector focus and responsibility.  His recent experience covers the Industrials, Healthcare, Technology, Real Estate, Infrastructure and FIG sectors.

Andrew Federer

Vice Chair

Back to Leadership

Andrew Federer is Vice Chairman, RBC Capital Markets and is a member of the Global Investment Banking Management Committee, the Equity Commitments Committee and the Mezzanine Finance Committee. He is responsible for senior client relationships and for providing advisory and deal execution services for the firm’s global clients, including: mergers and acquisitions, leveraged loan and high yield financings, bond issuance, and IPOs and secondary offerings.

Andrew has an extensive and broad range of transactional experience having advised a number of North America's largest corporate issuers and private equity firms. He also previously served as Head of Corporate Finance in Canada with responsibility for the management and direction of a number of teams, including: Communications, Media & Telecom, Financial Institutions, Consumer and Industrial Products, Financial Sponsors, Infrastructure Coverage, and Infrastructure (PPP) Project Finance.

Andrew is a member of the Board of Trustees of The Art Gallery of Ontario, Vice Chairman of the Board of Governors of The Bishops Strachan School and Co-Chairman of the RBC Capital Markets Foundation.

Kent Ferguson

Vice Chair

Back to Leadership

Kent Ferguson is Vice Chair, RBC Capital Markets and a member of the Global Investment Banking Management Committee. He leads senior client relationships and advises on a broad range of capital markets transactions – with particular focus on mining and resource clients and Canadian governments.

With over 25 years of investment banking experience, Kent brings extensive expertise in mergers and acquisitions, leveraged financings, activist defence and strategic repositioning. At RBC Capital Markets, he was instrumental in establishing the firm's leadership position in the oil and gas sector, serving as Co-Head of Canadian Energy (2014–2019) and Co-Head of Global Energy (2019–2023). In these roles, Kent managed senior client coverage and advised a number of North America's largest corporate issuers on strategic matters, capital markets transactions and industry initiatives spanning Indigenous equity, climate change policy, sustainable finance, environmental markets and energy transition.

Most recently as Senior Vice President, Strategy, Sustainability and Corporate Development at Suncor, Kent refined the company's long-term corporate strategy, spearheaded a refocus on capital-efficient oil sands project development and advanced industry advocacy initiatives. He oversaw project governance, technology development, industry associations, market forecasting, environmental stewardship and sustainability reporting, as well as indigenous and community relations.

Kent is a CFA charterholder and holds a Bachelor of Commerce degree from the University of Saskatchewan. He is a member of the Dean's Circle at the University of Saskatchewan’s Edwards School of Business, Previous board roles include Board Chair of United Way of Calgary and Area, director roles with the Canadian Association of Petroleum Producers, Pathways Alliance and Evok Innovations – a Canadian venture capital firm focused on cleantech and sustainability.

Back to Leadership
Michael Fortier

Vice Chair

Back to Leadership

Since October 2010, Michael Fortier is Vice Chairman, RBC Capital Markets. Prior to joining the Royal Bank of Canada, he had been active principally in the fields of banking, politics and law.

Over the past 25 years, Michael has worked as a senior relationship banker for several Wall Street (Morgan Stanley, Credit Suisse) and Canadian (TD Securities) investment banking firms and worked in Canada and the UK for one of the leading Canadian law firms (Norton Rose).

Between January 2006 and November 2008, Michael served as Canada's Minister of Public Works and Minister of International Trade. Throughout this period, he also acted as the Minister responsible for Greater Montreal. Michael also chaired Prime Minister Stephen Harper's Conservative Party leadership campaign in 2004 and the Party's 2004 and 2006 federal election campaigns.

Michael sits on the boards of CAE and Pomerleau. He also served from 2012 to 2015 as a member of United Technologies’ International Advisory Council. He is active with many philanthropic organizations, including as Chairman of Ste Justine Hospital’s Foundation since 2012. He has also accepted numerous pro bono assignments from municipal, provincial and federal governments, notably negotiating the return of Formula One racing to Canada.

Michael lives in Montreal with his wife Michelle and his six children.

Larry Grafstein

Deputy Chair

Back to Leadership

Larry Grafstein has been Deputy Chairman of Global Investment Banking at RBC Capital Markets since September of 2018. In his 30 years on Wall Street, he has advised clients on nearly $1 trillion of completed transactions. His experience spans all industries and geographies and includes some of the largest and most complex M&A, restructuring, equity and privatization deals.

His clients over the years have included AerCap, AT&T, BAT, Charter Communications, Creative Artists Agency, Fiat Chrysler Automobiles, Hutchison Whampoa, Intel, Jabil,  Juniper, Leucadia, Level 3, Microsoft, Mosaic, Sprint, Time Warner, TPG, Visteon and Vodafone.  Recently he advised CSX on its response to activist investor Mantle Ridge, IBM on its acquisition of Truven, and Molson Coors on its acquisition of its Miller Coors JV. He advised on the restructurings of WorldCom and Nortel, two of the largest done to date.   

He has worked on behalf of the Governments of Canada and Ontario regarding their investments in Chrysler and General Motors after the financial crisis and advised on the landmark privatizations of Telefonos de Mexico and Telstra of Australia. He recently represented Statewide Mobility Partners, a consortium of investment funds, on the divestiture of Indiana Toll Roads, one of the largest infrastructure sales in US history.  In 2014 he helped settle the strike and consumer boycott at Market Basket Supermarkets in New England through the sale by certain members of the Demoulas family of their ownership stake and resolution of their 20-year control dispute.

Larry is a graduate of Harvard University (B.A.), Oxford University (M.Phil, Balliol College, Rhodes Scholar), and the University of Toronto (J.D.). He is co-chair of his Harvard class and has served on the board of a number of public companies and philanthropic institutions, including the US board of Upper Canada College and the board of trustees of Horace Mann School in New York.

Back to Leadership
Caroline Mulroney

Vice Chair, RBC

Back to Leadership

Caroline Mulroney joined Royal Bank of Canada as Vice Chair in September 2026. She leads senior client relationships globally, connecting clients with RBC’s full breadth of capabilities in capital markets, commercial banking and wealth management, and advises the firm’s business leaders on the implications of evolving government policy, regulatory and public sector developments for clients.

Caroline brings more than 25 years of senior experience spanning Wall Street, international corporate law, Canadian investment management and government at the cabinet level.

Elected to the Ontario Legislature in 2018 and re-elected in 2022 and 2025, Caroline served on the Executive Council of Ontario for eight years in four senior portfolios. As President of the Treasury Board (2023 to 2026), she chaired the Cabinet subcommittee responsible for Ontario’s C$240 billion budget and fiscal plan, oversaw internal audit, risk management and accountability across government and more than 130 agencies, and led the adoption of AI solutions across the Ontario public sector to improve service delivery and value for money. As Minister of Transportation (2019 to 2023), she secured a historic intergovernmental agreement to fund the largest transit expansion plan in North America. She also served as Attorney General of Ontario and as Minister of Francophone Affairs (2018-2026).

Before her public service, Caroline built her career in financial services and law. She was Vice-President at BloombergSen Investment Partners where she oversaw regulatory compliance, client services and business development for a C$2 billion asset management firm and earlier advised a C$200 million venture debt fund at Wellington Financial LP. Caroline also served as Associate Director of the NYU Center for Law & Business and practised corporate law at Shearman & Sterling LLP in Manhattan. She began her career in investment banking at Bear, Stearns & Co. in New York.

Beyond her professional achievements, Caroline has been deeply engaged in her community, serving on the board of the Windsor-Detroit Bridge Authority, the Hospital for SickKids Foundation, the Fraser Institute and the National Theatre School of Canada. She co-founded national charity The Shoebox Project for Shelters and co-chaired the C$100 million campaign to establish the Brian Mulroney Institute of Government at St. Francis Xavier University.

Caroline graduated from NYU School of Law with a Juris Doctor and from Harvard College with a Bachelor of Arts. She holds the Chartered Investment Manager designation and is fully bilingual in English and French. She has been appointed Chevalier de la Légion d’honneur by the President of the French Republic and awarded the King Charles III Coronation Medal by the Government of Canada.

Blair Wark is Chief Financial Officer (CFO) for RBC in Asia-Pacific and Chief Operating Officer (COO), RBC Capital Markets Asia-Pacific. As CFO he leads the Asia-Pacific finance team and oversees all finance services to the Asia-Pacific business platforms, including valuations, financial and product control, and performance management. As COO, he oversees the regulatory obligations and business operations, and leads the functional, operational, and financial aspects of Capital Markets in the region. Blair is actively involved in regional diversity initiatives and is Chair of the Australia Diversity Council.

Sian Hurrell

Co-CEO, RBC Europe & Head, Capital Markets Europe

Back to Leadership

Sian Hurrell is Co-CEO Europe & Head, Capital Markets Europe.

As Co-CEO, Sian drives the strategic direction and oversight of the bank's European Capital Markets and Wealth Management businesses, spanning multiple jurisdictions and bringing together RBC's global capabilities to deliver integrated solutions for clients. As Head of Capital Markets Europe, Sian oversees a platform that combines deep regional expertise in Investment Banking, Corporate Banking and Global Markets, with the scale of a top 10 global investment bank. Capital Markets Europe serves major corporates, financial sponsors, Sovereigns, Supranationals and Agencies (SSAs), insurance companies, banks, asset managers and hedge funds, bringing together advice, capital, liquidity provision and market access to help clients achieve their objectives.

In her global sales, relationship management and structuring role, Sian leads client strategy and execution across Macro, Credit and Equity products for RBC Capital Markets’ Global Markets clients worldwide. With over 30 years of capital markets experience working with global corporate and institutional clients she has a proven track record of guiding clients through periods of market volatility and change, helping them to capitalise on market opportunities, and manage their hedging and investment objectives.

Since joining RBC in 2013, she has held senior leadership roles including Head of European Fixed Income and Currencies, Global Head of FX, and Head of Global Markets Europe. Prior to RBC, she led European Financial Institution Sales at Royal Bank of Scotland (now NatWest Markets).

Sian is a prominent industry voice shaping the future of financial markets. She has held leadership positions on the FICC Market Standards Board, the Bank of England's Joint FX Steering Committee, the Bank of Canada's Canadian Foreign Exchange Committee, and the International Capital Markets Association (ICMA). Most notably, she served seven years on the Board of the International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA), including as Chair of the Nominations Committee, helping to guide the evolution of global derivatives markets including LIBOR transition.

Sian holds a BA Hons degree from the University of Leeds in the UK.

Co-op / Internships - Canada - UK - US

RBC partners with many universities and colleagues to hire students across all business platforms, including Capital Markets. In Canada, we hire approximately 1,600 co-ops and summer interns every year across the RBC Enterprise, and we're retaining more and more of those students by offering them full-time opportunities upon graduation.

Over the course of your co-op placement or internship, you'll gain tangible, hands-on experience and insight into our business operations - where you'll be given real projects, with equal opportunity and challenges and achievement.

Exploring the Benefits

  • Gain meaningful work experience in a fast-paced, collaborative, and inclusive work environment to determine if that area of business is something you would like to pursue before committing full-time.

  • Partner with business leaders who support your development through coaching, mentoring and managing
  • Grow your professional network, which is extremely valuable for securing future employment

RBC Co-op Placements

RBC offers a variety of co-op placements during the Fall, Winter and Summer semesters, which can range from 4-months all the way to 16 months, depending on the program. Through these co-op work terms, RBC provides post-secondary students the opportunity to jumpstart your career early on and incorporate academic learning with paid work experience that alternates with study terms.

In addition to the benefits above, you will:

  • Enhance your skillset by jumping into training sessions that will prepare you for a successful co-op term
  • Explore different opportunities while creating relationships that ensure beyond your work term

RBC Summer Analyst Programs & Internships

RBC offers a variety of summer work experience opportunities in Capital Markets, which can range from 14 weeks to 16 weeks, depending on the opportunity. Students in their penultimate year of studies are eligible for our Summer Analyst Programs, while summer internships are open to all post-secondary students interested in Capital Markets.

In addition to the benefits above, you will:

  • Enhance your skillset by attending training that will prepare you for a successful summer internship
  • Explore different opportunities while creating relationships that ensure beyond your work term

We look for individuals who are constantly finding new ways to drive impact, always learning, and are able to adapt themselves so they can thrive in our new world of work.

Fixed Income Origination

Fixed Income Origination is a global practice within RBC Capital Markets that provides underwriting, capital-raising, liability management, ratings advisory, structuring expertise and execution to help our clients successfully raise debt in the primary and secondary markets. Our analysts help develop ideas and market insights to support the team in the origination, syndication and execution of corporate debt and securitization transactions across a number of industry groups.

Learn More

The group works closely with our investment banking, derivatives platform, equity capital markets, and sales and trading groups globally to achieve optimal execution for our clients. Being a banker within Fixed Income Origination is unique as you provide both product expertise and industry coverage to clients across different countries and currencies.

  • Debt Capital Markets (DCM) is consistently ranked as a leading originator and distributor of debt products. Whether our clients need to refinance operations, raise funds for an acquisition or restructure existing debt, we offer a powerful combination of global capabilities, sector knowledge and unrivalled execution, all backed by a strong balance sheet and one of the best credit ratings among global banks.
  • Securitization (Term ABS & Conduit Finance) offers attractive financing alternatives for companies that have current funding and liquidity needs. We work with clients to identify and convert future income streams – such as auto receivables, student loans and credit card receivables – into tradeable securities. We have extensive experience covering a wide range of traditional and non-traditional assets, as well as delivering innovative solutions and proprietary analytics.

Municipal Finance

Top Ranked Municipal Finance Department

RBC serves as underwriter and financial advisor for many State and local governments, not-for-profit hospitals and healthcare systems, universities and colleges, transportation agencies, power utilities, housing agencies, public infrastructure projects, and student loan programs. Our department is one of the largest and most active in the market as we number over 330 personnel with 182 municipal bankers across 27 locations throughout the US

We rank # 1 as the most active underwriter in terms of total senior managed negotiated financings over the past 10 years, while ranking # 1 by number of issues for 17 of the past 25 years.

Learn More

Municipal Finance Summer Analyst Program Overview

The Municipal Finance Summer Analyst provides analytical, research and transactional support to investment bankers and associates in all departmental work activities relating to the structuring and underwriting and issuance of negotiated bonds, and/or related financial advisory services.

The program provides a hands-on experience of public finance investment banking in which Summer Analysts will be directly involved in supporting book-run financings, preparing analysis for competitive proposal requests, as well as client service related analysis. Summer Analysts are considered generalists which will enable them to be staffed with multiple industry groups within the department to provide the broadest exposure possible. Summer Analysts can expect to develop their foundations in:

  • Preparing credit, operating and capital structure models and related financial analyses for potential and actual capital markets transactions
  • Organizing and analyzing information necessary to prepare proposals, client presentations, offering statements and marketing materials
  • Understanding and developing the ability to communicate financing alternatives in originating, structuring and marketing an issue and our firm wide capabilities
  • Economic, political and industry-specific forces affecting the issuance of municipal securities

Summer Analysts will benefit from the support of a mentor, a senior speaker series and a number of social events to facilitate networking and to discuss career opportunities.

Risk Management

RBC's Risk Management Function is responsible for the oversight of Market, Trading Credit and Liquidity Risk Management.

Learn More

The group uses a variety of measurement metrics and limits. Key responsibilities of Risk Management are:

  • Providing oversight of Market, Trading Credit and Liquidity Risk exposures
  • Transaction analysis and support
  • Quantifying and reporting the region's Market, Trading Credit and Liquidity Risk exposures using a wide variety of metrics and measurement tools such as Value-at-Risk, liquidity survival horizons, stress testing and "Greek" measures.
  • Establishing limits on Market, Trading Credit and Liquidity Risk exposures within the firm's risk appetite
  • Maintaining and implementing the necessary policies and procedures, including appropriate governance
  • Ensuring valuation models are used appropriately and in accordance with policy and approvals from our model vetting team
  • Risk policy development and Risk Capital Management

Patti Perras Shugart

Head, Global Corporate Banking

Patti Perras Shugart is Head, Global Corporate Banking and a member of the Operating Committee at RBC Capital Markets. In her role, Patti oversees a team of approximately 600 professionals globally who specialize in lending, trading credit, loan portfolio management and transaction banking for our corporate and institutional clients. She also chairs the Loan Portfolio Review Committee and the Commitments Committee which determine the firm’s global lending decisions.

Patti is a strong advocate for diversity and inclusion. She sits on the firm’s Capital Markets Global Diversity Leadership Council, is a co-founder of RWomen, a global internal forum dedicated to fostering and developing female talent, and she chairs VersaFi’s Advisory Council. She is RBC’s Executive Sponsor for the United Way’s Women United group, is a past United Way Cabinet Member, and a past Executive Champion for the Toronto RBC Race for the Kids. Patti has been recognized for her outstanding contributions to the industry through the VersaFi Visionary Award in 2025, the Champion of Change Award in 2016, and the Award for Leadership in 2010. She was also named one of Canada's Top 100 Most Powerful Women by Women's Executive Network in both 2015 and 2017.

Patti has an MBA from the University of Toronto (Rotman) and a Bachelor of Commerce (Honours) from Queen’s University.

Ralph Sehgal

Deputy Head, Global Corporate Banking

Ralph Sehgal is Deputy Head, Global Corporate Banking, a business with offices across Canada, the US, Europe and Australia. He also leads a team of professionals in Toronto, Montreal and Vancouver that provide client coverage across a broad range of industries and also sits on a number of internal committees, including the Corporate Banking/Global Credit Operating Committee and the loan Commitments Committee.

Prior to joining RBC Capital Markets in 2009, Ralph spent 13 years at CIBC World Markets in a number of roles, the most recent of which was Managing Director and Team Leader covering large corporate clients. Ralph also spent a number of years living and working abroad in Finland, Switzerland and England for Credit Suisse.

Ralph is a strong advocate for diversity and inclusion.  He is a National Executive Co-Sponsor of Mosaic, an employee resource group focused on promoting an inclusive environment within RBC Capital Markets.  Ralph was also named a Women in Capital Markets (now VersaFi) Champion of Change in 2023.

Ralph is a former member of the United Way Toronto's MIG Cabinet. He is a graduate of the University of Guelph holding a Combined Honors degree in Management and Economics, as well as Queen’s University where he earned a Master of Business Administration degree. Ralph also holds the Chartered Financial Analyst designation.

Jim Allred

Vice Chair, Power, Utilities & Infrastructure (PU&I)

Jim Allred is Vice Chair, Power, Utilities & Infrastructure (PU&I) for RBC Capital Markets. Jim joined RBC in 2008 and has over 35 years of corporate finance experience in the Energy industry. Previously, Jim has held senior management positions with Bank of America and Societe Generale as well as a position within the energy industry as Vice President and Treasurer of Link Energy, a crude oil gathering and transportation company.

Jim has served on educational and charitable boards including the Alumni Advisory Board of the McCombs School of Business at The University of Texas - Austin and the Forge for Families which assists underprivileged children in Houston. Jim graduated from the University of Texas in 1986 with a BBA degree in Finance.

Mike Gaudet

Global Head, Energy, Power, Utilities & Infrastructure (PU&I)

Mike Gaudet is Global Head Energy and Power, Utilities & Infrastructure (PU&I) at RBC Capital Markets. He leads a geographically distributed team across Calgary, Toronto, Houston, and New York, while maintaining close coordination with offices in London and Sydney. In this role, Mike oversees a comprehensive banking practice that partners with product and coverage teams to structure innovative debt financing solutions, execute complex transactions, and unlock the full breadth of RBC's capabilities for energy sector clients - driving long-term client relationships.

With 20 years at RBC Capital Markets, Mike brings deep expertise in debt related transactions and relationships. During his first decade with the firm, he led the structuring and execution of major non-recourse financings for energy and power infrastructure across North America.

Beyond his professional responsibilities, Mike serves on the Board of WinSport, a Calgary-based nonprofit that leverages the legacy of the 1988 Winter Olympics to advance inclusive, world-class athletic training opportunities.

Kathryn Ogden

Global Head, Real Estate Corporate Banking and Capital Partners (RECP)

Kathryn Ogden is Global Head, Real Estate Corporate Banking and Capital Partners (RECP) at RBC Capital Markets.

Kathryn joined RBC in 2009 in Dallas and was Head of Asset Management for the disposition of RBC’s legacy US real estate loan portfolio prior to helping launch the Real Estate Capital Partners platform in 2011. She moved to London in 2013 to launch the Real Estate Capital Partners platform in Europe before moving back to Dallas in 2016.

Prior to joining RBC, Kathryn worked in the London office of the Real Estate Principal Investment Area of Goldman, Sachs & Co. responsible for the management of a portfolio of real estate assets in the United Kingdom and Europe. Kathryn spent seven years with Goldman, Sachs & Co. in Dallas, Paris and London and has managed the financing, sale or initial public offering of real estate assets located in Canada, the United States and Europe.

Kathryn holds an honors degree in Business from The University of Texas at Austin.

Raja Khanna

U.S. Head, Corporate Banking

Raja Khanna is Head, U.S. Corporate Banking. He leads a team of senior bankers responsible for relationship management, cross-selling, and transaction execution across the credit ratings spectrum. Sectors covered include Industrials, Consumer, Healthcare, Municipals, Financial Institutions, Media, Telecommunications, and Technology. The Asset-Based Lending team also reports into Mr. Khanna.

He is a member of the Global Loan Commitments Committee, US Capital Markets Operating Committee, and Corporate Banking Global Operating Committee. He is a strong advocate for diversity and inclusion and serves as a member of the US Diversity Leadership Council, Executive Sponsor for RBC Mosaic (focused on promoting inclusion for minority groups), and a Board Member of the Hudson County Boys and Girls Club.

Mr. Khanna joined RBC in 2013, with over two decades of previous experience in investment banking at Barclays and Lehman Brothers and public accounting with Ernst & Young. He holds an MBA in Finance from the University of California, Berkeley, and a Master in Accounting and BSPH from the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill.

Edward Dickinson

Europe and Australia, Head, Corporate Banking & Global Head, Fund Finance

Mr. Dickinson joined RBC Capital Markets in March 2008 as Director in European Leveraged Finance. He was appointed head of European Leveraged Finance in 2017.

Mr. Dickinson remains co-head, European Leveraged Finance (a role he shares with Craig Campbell) and was appointed Managing Director and Head of UK & Europe and Australia Corporate Banking in April 2023.

From April 2009 to June 2010 Mr. Dickinson worked in the Toronto Leveraged Finance team on US and Canadian transactions. In September 2014, he assumed responsibility for the European High Yield Capital Markets. In 2016 he was appointed head of European Sponsor Coverage a role he relinquished in 2022.

From 2006 to 2008 he worked in the Origination and Execution offices for CIBC’s European Leveraged Finance department. Between 2003 and 2006, he worked in Calyon’s Leveraged Finance team in London.

Mr Dickinson gained his MBA at Cranfield Management School between 2002 and 2003 and prior to this was employed between 1996 and 2000 as a Lawyer in the London office of Morgan Lewis working in the corporate finance and banking teams on European and US transactions.

RBC Elements product evolution

RBC Elements has been redefining its capabilities and ushering in an era of AI-powered insight.

2018: RBC Elements launched

  • Formation of data science team embedded within Global Research.
  • First RBC Elements branded research note published, and featured in Bloomberg

2019: Research roll-out

  • Quick adoption within Research with publication of 70+ Elements-branded research notes

2020: Real time analytics in uncertain times

  • RBC Elements shifts from a focus on forecasting the future to analyzing market events in real-time, raising conviction through nowcasting
  • Proprietary analysis such as “RBC Sheds Light on Chinas Rebound After Coronavirus” also featured in WSJ

2021: RBC Elements diversifies product suite

  • Digital Intelligence Strategy (DIS), a thematic macro research product centered on ‘nowcasting’ trends from structured & unstructured datasets, established
  • Launch of Next-gen applications, a new interactive web based channel that allows that allows the ability to directly interact with the data and models behind some of our key RBC Elements Research products

2022: RBC Elements scales and forays beyond research

  • RBC Elements starts to process over 7.5 billion unique, real-time datapoints to assist research, and our clients in their investment process
  • New Capital Markets solutions Beyond Research
    • Launch of the QIS Commodity Sentiment Strategy, a Machine Learning model that provides trading signals using social media data

2023: New business onboarding

  • Expansion of Capital Markets solutions Beyond Research
  • Launch of Central Bank AI Sight™, an AI powered sentiment analysis tool, trained to decipher cues from Central Bank communications
  • RBC Elements embeds within Global Investment Banking

2024: Continued product growth & data solutions

  • Approaching 1000 RBC Elements research publications and 15 Next-Gen Applications live on RBC Insight
  • Continuous development of strategy and proprietary products housed under the RBC Elements™ brand

Matthew R. Stopnik

Global Head, Investment Banking, RBC Capital Markets

Matthew Stopnik is Head, Global Investment Banking. He joined RBC Capital Markets in January 2015 as the Co-Head of Financial Sponsors. Prior to joining RBC, Matthew spent 20 years at UBS Investment Bank where his most recent role was serving as its U.S. Head of Financial Sponsors.

At RBC, Matthew is responsible for U.S. Investment Banking. He shares responsibility for coverage of banking clients and prospects, including corporate finance industry groups, mergers and acquisitions, equity capital markets, leveraged finance, and loan and high-yield capital markets teams. Matthew is also responsible for managing RBC’s relationships with some of the largest and most active private equity firms in the world. He serves on the firm’s Global Capital Markets and U.S. Regional Operating Committees and he is a member of the firm’s Commitments Committee.

Matthew is Vice Chair and a member of the Board of Trustees of the TEAK Fellowship, a member of the Board of Youth, INC. and a David Rockefeller Fellow of the Partnership for New York City. He received a B.A from the University of Michigan. Matthew and his wife live in New York City with their two children.

Trevor Gardner

Head, Global Investment Banking Coverage, RBC Capital Markets

Trevor Gardner is Head, Global Investment Banking Coverage and a member of the Capital Markets Operating Committee at RBC Capital Markets. With more than 25 years of capital markets experience at RBC, Trevor has held roles across Investment Banking and Equity Capital Markets in Toronto and Calgary. He was previously Head of Canadian Investment Banking and Co-Head of Canadian Energy Investment Banking.

Trevor brings extensive experience advising clients on a broad range of transactions, including mergers and acquisitions as well as debt and equity financing. He is actively engaged in senior client coverage and provides advice to clients across industries.

Trevor is an executive member of RBC Capital Markets' Canadian Diversity Leadership Council. Beyond his professional responsibilities, Trevor is deeply involved in community initiatives, serving as Chair of Right To Play's Canadian Advisory Board and Chair of the Board of Directors for YMCA Calgary. He is also a member of the Dean's Advisory Council for the Lazaridis School of Business and Economics at Wilfrid Laurier University.

Originally from Saskatchewan, Trevor holds a Bachelor of Business Administration (Honours) from Wilfrid Laurier University and is a Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA).

Jim Wolfe

Head, Global Investment Banking Capital Markets, RBC Capital Markets

Jim Wolfe is Head, Global Investment Banking Capital Markets, overseeing the firm’s financing products across debt and equity in both the public and private markets.

Prior to assuming his current role in May 2024, Jim served as Co-Head of U.S. Investment Banking from 2018-2024, where he shared responsibility for the coverage of banking clients and prospects, as well as oversight of the industry sector coverage groups, mergers and acquisitions, equity capital markets, leveraged finance and loan and high-yield capital markets teams.

From 2008 to 2018, Jim was responsible for the firm’s leveraged finance business in the U.S and Europe, leading an experienced team of specialized professionals in raising capital for corporate acquisitions, leveraged buyouts, recapitalizations and refinancings. Jim also serves on the Global Capital Markets Operating Committee and is a member of the firm’s Commitments and Underwriting Distribution Committees. He joined RBC in June 2008 after a 15-year tenure at Bear Stearns where he served as a Senior Managing Director in the Leveraged Finance Group.

With over 32 years of experience, Jim has successfully executed transactions of all sizes across a broad range of industry sectors.

Jim holds a B.S. in Accounting from the University of Southern California and an MBA from The Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania. He served on the Board of Trustees at Greens Farms Academy in Westport, CT, from 2012 to 2018, and alongside his wife, chaired the Parents Executive Committee of Bowdoin College from 2014 to 2019.

Ben Mandell

Head, Global Mergers & Acquisitions, RBC Capital Markets

Ben Mandell is Head, Global Mergers & Acquisitions at RBC Capital Markets. He has been in the M&A group at RBC over 10 years with prior experience working at an independent financial advisory firm in Toronto, in the Investment Management Division at Goldman Sachs in both New York and Toronto as well as working as a Consultant with Monitor Group in London.

Ben received his Bachelor’s degree in Economics from Queen’s University, an MBA from Harvard Business School and he holds the CFA designation.

Dominic Hudson

Head, Investment Banking, Europe and APAC

Dominic Hudson is Head, Investment Banking, leading our investment banking sector, product and country teams across Europe and APAC, and is a member of the RBC Capital Markets Operating Committee.

Dominic is responsible for executing the regional growth strategy for our investment banking franchises in Europe and APAC, focused on achieving our client, revenue and market share goals, building upon our existing robust client franchise and deepening our incredibly strong bench of talent.

Dominic began his career as a chartered accountant at Ernst & Young. He then held roles at Deutsche Bank and Rothschild before joining RBC in 2006 to lead our infrastructure, transport and utilities team in Australia. In 2012, he was appointed as Head of Investment Banking Asia-Pacific and then chief country officer Head for RBC Capital Markets Australia in 2015.

Dominic was appointed to the newly-created position of Head of European Sector Coverage in 2018, relocating to the UK. In this role, he was instrumental in the growth of our ten industry teams providing strong connectivity across sectors, products and European country teams, before assuming his current role of Head of Investment Banking, Europe and APAC in November 2022.

Jonathan Hunter

Head, Global Markets

Jonathan Hunter is Head, Global Markets for RBC Capital Markets, and has been a member of the RBC Capital Markets Operating Committee since 2008. He is also on the board of RBC’s U.S. Intermediate Holding Company (IHC).

Jonathan has been with RBC for more than 30 years, joining its Dealer Trainee Program in 1991. Since then, he has held progressively senior roles within Capital Markets, including Global Co-Head, Fixed Income and Currencies (2006-2011), based in New York, and Global Head of Liquid Products (2002-2006), based in London. He most recently held the role of Global Head of Fixed Income, Currencies and Commodities since 2011 before his appointment to Head of Global Markets in November 2020.

Today, Jonathan leads a team of close to 2,000 professionals within Global Markets, collectively comprised of Sales & Relationship Management, Digital Solutions & Client Insights, Central Funding, Equities, Spread, and Macro business lines. Global Markets is a significant contributor to RBC Capital Markets earnings, and is focused on driving best-in-class client solutions across multiple asset classes through digital innovation and thought leadership.

Jonathan recently completed an eight-year term as a member of the Board of the International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA).

Jonathan is also actively involved in RBC’s diversity, mentorship and recruitment initiatives, and is a member of RBC Capital Markets’ Canadian Diversity Leadership Council. In 2018, he was formally recognized by the Women in Capital Markets organization as a Champion of Change in acknowledgement for his ongoing efforts to advance women in the workplace.

In addition, Jonathan is a key participant and contributor in RBC’s many community and charitable initiatives, including the RBC Race for the Kids, RBC Trade for the Kids, and he serves as a member of the United Way’s Major Individual Givers cabinet as part of RBC’s annual Employee Giving Campaign.

With Jonathan’s focus on digital transformation, he was recently named to the Advisory Board of the newly designed Smith’s Master of Financial Innovation & Technology (MFIT) program at Queen’s University. He also served as Chair of the Board of Trustees, and sat on the Board of Governors, for The Bishop Strachan School in Toronto from 2015 to 2021.

Jonathan earned his Honours Bachelor of Commerce Degree (Finance) from Queen’s University in 1991, and is a Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA).

Ivan Bandic

Global Head, Capital Markets Treasury

Ivan Bandic is Global Head, Capital Markets Treasury and both a member of the Global Markets Operating Committee as well as the Enterprise Corporate Treasury Operating Committee.

In this role, Ivan leads the management of Enterprise’s short-term funding and liquidity needs, oversees the Capital Markets Liquidity Asset Portfolio, and optimizes Capital Markets financial resources, including the management of derivative-related XVAs (credit and funding risks).

Since joining RBC Capital Markets in 2004, Ivan has held increasingly senior positions spanning risk management, trading and treasury functions. His career progression includes roles as Head of Portfolio Optimization in Rates Trading (2012), Global Head of Resources Management (2016) – which consolidated financial resources, collateral management and XVA trading across the organization – and Global Head of CM Treasury (2023), each expanding his mandate to address evolving Capital Markets priorities.

Ivan holds a Master’s degree in Mathematics from the University of British Columbia and is a CFA charter holder. He lives in Toronto with his wife and two children.

Jim Byrd

Global Head, Macro Products

Jim Byrd is Global Head, Macro Products at RBC Capital Markets.

Jim began his career with RBC in Toronto as part of the Global Markets Training Program before a five-year stint in RBC’s London office. Jim was named Managing Director in 2006 before becoming Head of Canadian and then Global Rates in 2017. In 2021 Jim was appointed Global Head of Macro Products and is responsible for RBC’s Rates, Commodities, Foreign Exchange and Futures businesses.

Alongside the Deputy Governor of the Bank of Canada, Jim co-chairs the Canadian Fixed Income Forum (CFIF) and is executive sponsor of RBC Pride in support of LGBTQ+ initiatives within Capital Markets. In 2023, Jim co-chaired the Global RBC Employee Giving Campaign and in 2024 was named one of Versa-Fi’s Champions of Change for being a leader in advancing equity in the workplace.

Jim is a native of Newfoundland and graduated from Memorial University in 1995 with a Bachelor of Commerce degree and is a CFA charterholder.

He lives in Toronto with his wife and two children.

Derek Flood

Global Head, Cash Equities and Research

Derek Flood is Global Head, Cash Equities and Research at RBC Capital Markets.

Derek has been with RBC since 1995, working in a variety of roles at the firm, including in Corporate Finance with Investment Banking and the Institutional Equity Group. He is responsible for delivering global equity products and capabilities to RBC’s institutional client base.

Derek is an Executive Sponsor for RBC Capital Markets’ RWomen Canada employee resource group and was co-chair of the RBC Capital Markets Canadian Diversity Leadership Council from 2015 to 2019. He is a member of the RBC Capital Markets Foundation Committee and he serves on the Board of Capitalize for Kids and Baycrest Foundation. 

Derek graduated from Queen’s University in 1995 with a Bachelor of Arts (Honours Economics) degree and from the Richard Ivey School of Business in 2000 with a Masters of Business Administration degree. He and his family live in Toronto. 

Sian Hurrell

Co-CEO, RBC Europe & Europe Head, Capital Markets, RBC Capital Markets

Sian Hurrell is Co-CEO Europe & Head, Capital Markets Europe.

As Co-CEO, Sian drives the strategic direction and oversight of the bank's European Capital Markets and Wealth Management businesses, spanning multiple jurisdictions and bringing together RBC's global capabilities to deliver integrated solutions for clients. As Head of Capital Markets Europe, Sian oversees a platform that combines deep regional expertise in Investment Banking, Corporate Banking and Global Markets, with the scale of a top 10 global investment bank. Capital Markets Europe serves major corporates, financial sponsors, Sovereigns, Supranationals and Agencies (SSAs), insurance companies, banks, asset managers and hedge funds, bringing together advice, capital, liquidity provision and market access to help clients achieve their objectives.

In her global sales, relationship management and structuring role, Sian leads client strategy and execution across Macro, Credit and Equity products for RBC Capital Markets’ Global Markets clients worldwide. With over 30 years of capital markets experience working with global corporate and institutional clients she has a proven track record of guiding clients through periods of market volatility and change, helping them to capitalise on market opportunities, and manage their hedging and investment objectives.

Since joining RBC in 2013, she has held senior leadership roles including Head of European Fixed Income and Currencies, Global Head of FX, and Head of Global Markets Europe. Prior to RBC, she led European Financial Institution Sales at Royal Bank of Scotland (now NatWest Markets).

Sian is a prominent industry voice shaping the future of financial markets. She has held leadership positions on the FICC Market Standards Board, the Bank of England's Joint FX Steering Committee, the Bank of Canada's Canadian Foreign Exchange Committee, and the International Capital Markets Association (ICMA). Most notably, she served seven years on the Board of the International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA), including as Chair of the Nominations Committee, helping to guide the evolution of global derivatives markets including LIBOR transition.

Sian holds a BA Hons degree from the University of Leeds in the UK.

Rod Ireland

Head, Asia, RBC Wealth Management & Head, Global Markets, APAC, RBC Capital Markets & CEO, RBC Singapore Branch

Rod Ireland is head, RBC Wealth Management – Asia. In this role, Rod is responsible for the wealth management businesses based in Hong Kong and Singapore. In addition, he is head of Global Markets APAC. 

An accomplished business leader, Rod leads the Global Markets businesses across the APAC region (Australia, Singapore, Japan), with responsibilities including managing key client relationships across financials, corporates, asset managers and government agencies and ranging from group treasurers, CIOS and CEOs. Rod is also responsible for effective governance and regulatory oversight for RBC’s activities in Singapore.

Since joining RBC in 1998, Rod has been pivotal in driving and executing strategies that have established RBC as a tier one organization in a number of global markets businesses across the APAC region.

Matthew Ouderkirk

Chief Operating Officer, Global Markets

Matt Ouderkirk is Chief Operating Officer, Global Markets at RBC Capital Markets.

Matt joined RBC in 2026 and brings more than 20 years of capital markets experience across client-facing and operational roles. He is a member of both the Global Markets Operating Committee and the U.S. Capital Markets Operating Committee. In his role, he partners with senior leaders and business teams to drive strategic alignment across front- and back-office functions, technology and risk management. He focuses on translating business strategy into operational excellence, optimizing execution capabilities and building robust governance frameworks that strengthen competitive positioning and unlock revenue opportunities across Global Markets.

Prior to joining RBC, Matt served as COO of UBS Investment Bank Americas, where he executed regional strategy, strengthened governance and operational risk management and drove new business initiatives. His earlier career included institutional credit sales at Goldman Sachs – an experience that shaped his client-first lens on how operational and risk decisions ultimately affect the firms and investors RBC serves.

Matt holds a bachelor's degree in Computer Science from Colgate University. He leverages this technical foundation alongside his deep market experience to ensure RBC balances technological innovation with commercial effectiveness – translating complex capabilities into tangible business value. He splits his time between Manhattan and Long Island with his partner and Wheaten Terrier.

Daniel Rosenbaum

Head, Central Funding

Daniel Rosenbaum is Head, Central Funding (CFG) business division and Chairman of the RBC (Barbados) Trading Bank Corporation and RBC CMA LLC subsidiaries. As the Head of CFG, Daniel is responsible for overseeing a global secured financing business which delivers balance sheet solutions to its clients as well as managing investment and market making strategies.

Daniel joined RBC Capital Markets in 1999 in New York as member of the firm's Global Arbitrage and Trading business. He was transferred to London in 2000 where he developed a European trading business as well as co-founded the CFG business. In 2005 he relocated to the Bahamas to develop the firm's Caribbean platform before being transferred back to New York in 2010. 

Daniel holds a BS in Mathematics from the University of California, Santa Barbara and a MS in Operations Research from Princeton University.

Jeremy Sonnenburg

Head, Quantitative and Technology Services

Jeremy Sonnenburg is Global Head, Quantitative and Technology Services (QTS) and serves as the line of business CIO for RBC Capital Markets (RBCCM). He and the QTS team are responsible for all software applications and quantitative analytics used by the Capital Markets division. 

Jeremy joined RBC in 2010 as the Global Head of Commodities Technology. Since joining RBC, Jeremy has held several technology leadership roles in CM with increasing responsibility. At RBC, Jeremy sits on the Global Markets Operating Committee (GMOC), the T&O Operating Committee (T&O OC), and the US Diversity Leadership Committee (USDLC). He is also a regular guest at the Capital Markets Operating Committee (CMOC).

Prior to RBC, Jeremy held senior roles to drive change at Barclays Capital and Credit Suisse. He started his career as a consultant at Andersen Consulting (now Accenture) working as a technology consultant in financial sector and the Energy Downstream Wholesale Trading sector. Jeremy is a graduate of the McCombs School of Business at the University of Texas in Austin where he studied Management of Information Systems.

Lindsay Patrick

Chief Strategy & Innovation Officer

Lindsay Patrick is Head, Strategy, Marketing and Sustainability at RBC Capital Markets and a member of the firm’s Operating Committee.

Lindsay is responsible for the advancement of the RBC Capital Markets’ business, brand, and marketing strategy, supporting the firm’s overall growth and performance ambitions. She is a senior adviser on ESG matters to the Group Executive and the wider RBC enterprise, providing insight and guidance in respect of our Capital Markets client base and the transition to net zero. Lindsay also oversees the Sustainable Finance Group, and with her global team, spearheads the provision of solutions and advice for RBC’s institutional and corporate clients across all areas of sustainable finance that incorporates both environmental and social perspectives.

Lindsay has over two decades experience in investment banking, spanning trading floors across North America, Europe, Australia, and Asia. She began her career with RBC Capital Markets in Investment Banking in Toronto and spent 10 years across variety of positions in Global Equities with a global bank in London before returning to RBC Capital Markets in 2016.

Lindsay is passionate about talent development and is active in advancing important initiatives related to Diversity and Inclusion.  Within RBC, she is a mentor to numerous colleagues, supporting their growth and development across the bank.

Lindsay received her MBA with Honours in Finance from The Wharton School at the University of Pennsylvania, her BBA with Honours in International Business from Bishop’s University, is a CFA Charterholder and completed the CFA Certificate in ESG Investing. Lindsay sits on the Advisory Board for the Institute of Sustainable Finance and is recognized as leader in sustainability in Canada as a Clean50 Honoree. She is an active volunteer within her local community and serves on the Board Directors for the Oakville Community Foundation. Lindsay is married and the proud mother of four boys.

Sarah Thompson

Global Head, Sustainable Finance

Sarah Thompson leads RBC Capital Markets' Sustainable Finance Group, advising institutional, corporate, and government clients on integrating sustainability into their capital markets strategies and financial disclosures.

Since joining RBC in 2011 as the bank's first Green IT Manager, Sarah has progressed through several sustainability roles, including directing enterprise-wide operational footprint reduction, overseeing sustainability disclosures, and developing sustainable finance products and services. She was instrumental in establishing RBC's Green Bond Program in 2019 and Sustainable Commercial Paper Program in 2022.

Sarah represents RBC Capital Markets on the International Sustainability Standards Board Investor Advisory Group. She previously served on Canada's Sustainable Finance Action Council Taxonomy Technical Expert Group and currently serves on the Financial Services Advisory Group, advancing Canada's sustainable investment guidelines.

Sarah holds a Bachelor of Commerce in Economics from McGill University and an MBA in Sustainability from York University’s Schulich School of Business. She is based in Toronto, Canada.

Moses Choi

U.S. Head, Sustainable Finance

As part of the Sustainable Finance Group within RBC Capital Markets, Moses collaborates with corporate and institutional clients to deliver innovative sustainable finance solutions that integrate environmental, social and governance (ESG) factors. He joined the firm in 2021 with a focus on U.S. Capital Markets opportunities. Prior to joining RBC Capital Markets, Moses was Head of Digital and Sustainable Finance within the corporate strategy and venture team at Orange, where he advised on the telecommunications company’s inaugural €500m Sustainability Bond issuance and led sustainable and impact investing opportunities. Before Orange, Moses spent ten years in capital markets, corporate and investment banking, and sustainable finance at Citigroup Global Markets and Morgan Stanley. Moses holds BA and BSc degrees from Cornell University and a master’s degree from the Fletcher School at Tufts University with a focus on sustainable development.

Stefano Vitali

European Head, Sustainable Finance

Stefano Vitali leads the bank’s UK and European Sustainable Finance efforts to deliver innovative ESG solutions for corporate and institutional clients. Stefano leverages on over 10 years of experience in renewable energy, project finance and debt capital market and sustainable finance. Stefano joined the team in 2022 from UniCredit, where he previously structured pioneering sustainable finance solutions in sectors such as Energy and Utilities, Infrastructure, Healthcare and Financial Institutions. Stefano holds a Master of Science degree from Bocconi University with a focus on finance and financial markets.

Brian Hong

Director, Environmental Markets Solutions Group

Brian Hong leads the Environmental Markets Solutions Group within RBC Capital Markets. In his role, Brian supports clients looking to operationalize their net-zero targets through bespoke renewable energy and carbon solutions. Brian joined RBC in 2013 and worked in corporate strategy before pursuing a career change to focus on sustainability. Following graduate school, Brian returned to RBC and joined the Corporate Sustainability team where he led RBC’s carbon neutrality and renewable energy strategy, environmental reporting and the development of the first-ever renewable energy power purchase agreement signed by a financial institution in Canada. Brian previously worked in the Capital Markets Sustainable Finance Group where he led the integration of sustainability factors into Capital Markets’ core businesses globally by providing advice and developing solutions across all areas of sustainable finance for corporate and institutional clients. Brian holds a Master of Science in Sustainability Management from Columbia University and an Honours in Business Administration from the Ivey Business School.

Dana Hummel

Vice President, Sustainable Finance

As part of the Sustainable Finance Group within RBC Capital Markets, Dana is responsible for driving the integration of environmental, social and governance (ESG) factors into RBC Capital Markets Corporate Client and Global Markets advisory businesses. Dana joined RBC in 2017 in Corporate Banking in New York covering the Consumer & Retail sector, working closely with the Sustainable Finance Group to integrate ESG considerations into corporate lending. Previously, Dana worked in ESG consulting for asset management firms and in sell-side credit research covering the banking sector at Bank of America Merrill Lynch and Goldman Sachs. Dana holds a Graduate Certificate in Sustainable Finance from Columbia University and Bachelor’s Degree in Finance from Virginia Tech, and is a SASB FSA Credential Holder.

TULSA, Okla., Sept. 10, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) - ONEOK, Inc. today announced the closing of the previously announced $9 billion minority equity investment by funds and affiliates managed by Apollo.

Under the terms of the agreement, Apollo has invested $9 billion in exchange for a nonvoting Class B minority interest in a newly formed holding company, ONEOK Holdings, L.L.C., which is structurally subordinate to the company’s debt.

The minority equity investment has been reviewed with ONEOK's credit rating agencies, all of which consider the transaction credit-enhancing.
